title: Revealed Ambition and the Transition through Education
abstract: Howdemanding a qualification should students choose relative to their academic ability? We argue that this choice reveals ambition and study howthe choice relates to later outcomes. Linking PISA2012 data for Switzerland to administrative records,we followstudents for more than ten years. We measure revealed ambition as the difference between the median PISA score of entrants to a student’s chosen upper secondary qualification and the student’s own score. Qualifications encompass more than 200 vocational occupations and several general education programmes with widely varying academic requirements. Consistent with our interpretation, revealed ambition is associated, conditional on ability, with socioeconomic background and, strongly, with the occupational status that students expect to hold at age 30. The results reveal a trade-off: ambitious students are less likely to complete upper secondary education on time, but more likely to obtain a tertiary degree. Among vocational students, they also earn more.

title: The Value of Practical Skills
abstract: Practical skills are believed to affect labor market success, yet evidence is scarce because they are occupation-specific and difficult to measure. We use high-stakes expert evaluations of apprentices’ performance in standardized practical examinations across more than 170 occupations, held under authentic workplace conditions and linked to administrative records, to separate practical skills from general and vocational knowledge. Practical skills form a distinct dimension of human capital, weakly correlated with conventional achievement measures. They are associated with higher first-year earnings, lower NEET risk, greater retention by training firms, and tertiary entry. Out-of-sample, they substantially improve prediction beyond achievement and background characteristics.
